en: to fling off; to throw away

examples.en: As soon as I got home, I flung off my coat.
It's so hot that I want to throw off my coat.
Now try to shake off your old prejudices.
The child kicked off his shoes and ran to the sea.

examples.ko: 그는 체면을 벗어던진 채 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: He cast aside his dignity and danced.
Don't just fling your socks off; put them in the laundry basket.

explain: 옷이나 신발을 거칠게 벗어 던질 때도 쓰고, 편견·체면·걱정 같은 추상적인 것을 떨쳐 버릴 때도 써요. 그냥 '벗다'보다 힘 있고 시원한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I kicked off my shoes and lay down on the sofa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 거칠게 벗어서 던지듯 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when roughly taking something off and tossing it aside.

phrases.en: If you throw off your prejudice, you'll make more friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 생각을 완전히 버린다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to completely cast off a bad way of thinking.

phrases.en: Throw off your worries and enjoy your trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 부담을 시원하게 떨쳐 버릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shaking off a mental burden with a sense of relief.

explain_en: It is used for taking off clothes or shoes roughly and tossing them aside, and also for shaking off abstract things such as prejudice, dignity or worries. It feels more forceful and liberating than plain '벗다'.

en: nursing care; caring for a sick person

examples.en: I took leave to take care of my mother during her illness.

examples.ko: 며칠째 병간호를 하느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I haven't slept for days because I've been nursing someone.
Nursing a patient is hard on the family.
My father was hospitalized, so my older sister took charge of his care.

examples.ko: 병간호에 지친 가족을 위해 간병인을 구했어요.
examples.en: We hired a caregiver for the family worn out from nursing.
After a long period of nursing, my grandmother recovered.

explain: '병간호를 하다/맡다'처럼 써요. 가족이 아픈 사람을 곁에서 돌보는 일에 많이 쓰고, 직업으로 하는 사람은 '간병인'이라고 해요. 동사로는 '간호하다'나 '돌보다'도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My older brother is in charge of caring for our mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 그 일을 책임지는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say who takes responsibility for the care.

phrases.en: I took care of my sick child all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병간호'와 뜻이 가까운 동사예요. 아픈 사람을 곁에서 돌본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb close in meaning to 병간호: to look after a sick person at their side.

phrases.en: We hired a caregiver at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병간호를 직업으로 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who does nursing care as a job.

explain_en: Common everyday word for caring for a sick person, at home or in hospital. It is used as '병간호를 하다/맡다', most often for family members looking after a sick person. A professional who does this is called a '간병인'. As verbs, '간호하다' and '돌보다' are also common.

t90.ax: Nursing a patient is hard on the family.

en: to support someone by the arm; to help someone walk

examples.en: I supported Grandma at her side so she wouldn't fall.

examples.ko: 다리를 다친 친구를 부축해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I supported my friend, who hurt his leg, and we went to the hospital.
Please help the elderly person on the stairs.
He walked while supporting his stumbling father.
I'll support you, so please get up slowly.

examples.ko: 아픈 동생을 부축하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see him supporting his sick younger sibling.

explain: 몸이 불편한 사람의 팔이나 몸을 잡고 걷거나 일어나게 도울 때 써서, 그냥 '돕다'보다 동작이 구체적이에요. 어르신께는 '부축해 드리다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I helped my grandfather by supporting his arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신께 쓰는 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Honorific form for elders.

phrases.en: My father walked with my support.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 받는 사람 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the point of view of the person helped.

phrases.en: I helped the fallen child up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넘어진 사람을 일으킬 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for helping a fallen person up.

explain_en: It is used when you hold someone's arm or body so they can walk or stand, which makes it more physical than plain '돕다'. For an elder, say '부축해 드리다'.

dis.h: hold someone's arm to steady them
gh: help someone; do a favor for them
help; basic verb, takes a direct object
assist in a supporting role; subsidize

p.n: The replacement is vague and does not mean physically holding her arm.

examples.ko: 열이 나서 비틀비틀 걸어 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I had a fever, so I staggered to the hospital.

examples.ko: 아기가 비틀비틀 걷다가 엄마 품에 안겼어요.
examples.en: The baby toddled unsteadily and fell into its mom's arms.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 비틀비틀하며 겨우 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: I was so tired that I stumbled along and barely made it home.
He rose unsteadily and then sat back down.
The ship was rocking, so people walked unsteadily.

examples.ko: 자전거를 처음 탈 때는 비틀비틀 흔들려요.
examples.en: When you first ride a bike, you wobble from side to side.

explain: 몸이 힘이 없거나 균형을 잃어서 이리저리 흔들리는 모습에 써요. 동사 '비틀거리다'와 함께 외우면 좋고, 뒤에 '걷다, 일어서다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: A drunk person is walking while staggering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비틀비틀'과 짝을 이루는 동사로, 실제 흔들리는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that pairs with '비틀비틀', describing the actual swaying movement.

phrases.en: I was so tired that I walked unsteadily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 없어서 균형을 잃은 걸음걸이에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an unbalanced gait due to weakness.

phrases.en: I fell and then got up unsteadily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일어서는 순간 몸이 흔들리는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the body wobbling at the moment of standing up.

explain_en: Unsteady walking from drunkenness, weakness, or blindfold; losing balance. It describes a body swaying back and forth when weak or off balance. It is good to learn it with the verb '비틀거리다', and it is often followed by words like '걷다' (walk) and '일어서다' (stand up).

examples.en: The plan went rocky from the start, so I was worried.
I can hear the old door creaking.
The teamwork is shaky.
The bed creaked all night.

examples.ko: 마루가 삐걱댈 때마다 할아버지 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Every time the floor creaks, I think of my grandfather.

examples.ko: 일이 삐걱대도 포기하지 말고 다시 해 봐요.
examples.en: Even if things go rocky, don't give up and try again.

explain: 문이나 마루가 내는 소리에도 쓰고, 일이나 사이가 순조롭지 않을 때 비유로도 많이 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '삐걱거리다'도 써요.

phrases.example: 결혼 후 부부 사이가 삐걱대기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: The relationship starts to creak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람이나 조직의 관계가 순조롭지 않고 서로 맞지 않는 상태를 소리에 빗대어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It compares a strained relationship between people or within a group to a creaking sound, meaning things are not running smoothly.

explain_en: Shorter variant of the longer form (삐거덕대다); same creaking sound. It is used for the sound of doors or floors, and also figuratively when work or a relationship is not going smoothly. '삐걱거리다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: It snowed a lot, so I've been shoveling since morning.
I'm digging with a shovel to plant potatoes in the garden.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 삽질해서 손에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I shoveled all day, so I got blisters on my hands.

examples.ko: 설명서도 안 보고 하다가 괜히 삽질했네요.
examples.en: I didn't read the manual and ended up wasting effort for nothing.

examples.ko: 또 삽질하기 싫으면 처음부터 자료를 꼼꼼히 확인하세요.
examples.en: If you don't want to waste effort again, check the materials carefully from the start.

examples.ko: 방법을 몰라서 혼자 삽질하다가 결국 선배한테 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I didn't know how, so after flailing around alone I finally asked my senior.

explain: 원래는 삽으로 땅을 파거나 눈을 치우는 일이지만, 요즘 입말에서는 방법을 몰라서 헛수고를 하거나 쓸데없이 시간을 낭비했을 때도 써요. 친구끼리 가볍게 쓰는 말이라 윗사람에게는 '헛수고하다'가 더 안전해요.

phrases.en: I dug the ground with a shovel and planted a tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 뜻을 풀어서 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that spells out the original meaning of shoveling.

phrases.en: I cleared snow in front of the apartment this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삽으로 눈을 치우는 일을 가리킬 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for clearing snow with a shovel.

phrases.en: I didn't read the instructions, so it was all wasted effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삽질하다'의 헛수고 뜻과 같지만 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as the 'wasted effort' sense of '삽질하다', but safe to use with superiors.

explain_en: Literally it means digging the ground or clearing snow with a shovel, but in today's spoken Korean it is also used when you waste effort or time because you didn't know the right way. It is casual talk among friends, so '헛수고하다' is safer with someone senior.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 생떼를 써요.
examples.en: The child throws a tantrum, demanding I buy the toy.

examples.ko: 생떼 쓰지 말고 이유를 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't be unreasonable; tell me your reason.

examples.ko: 생떼에 못 이겨 결국 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I couldn't stand the nagging and ended up buying it for him.

examples.ko: 동생의 생떼가 시작되면 아무도 못 말려요.
examples.en: Once my younger sibling starts being stubborn, nobody can stop it.
He insists unreasonably, but he has no evidence.

examples.ko: 그렇게 생떼만 부리면 아무도 도와주지 않아요.
examples.en: If you only act unreasonably like that, nobody will help you.

explain: '생떼를 쓰다/부리다'로 짝지어 쓰고, 안 되는 일을 막무가내로 조르거나 우길 때 말해요. '떼를 쓰다'보다 억지스러운 느낌이 더 강하고, 아이뿐 아니라 어른에게도 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 과자를 사 달라고 생떼를 써요.
phrases.en: The child insists unreasonably that I buy snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 대표적인 짝말이에요. 안 되는 일을 계속 우길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical pairing, for stubbornly insisting on something impossible.

phrases.example: 동생이 게임을 더 하겠다고 생떼를 부려요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling insists unreasonably on playing more games.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생떼를 쓰다'와 뜻이 같고 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '생떼를 쓰다' and interchangeable with it.

phrases.en: Please don't make unreasonable demands here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게도 쓸 수 있지만 꽤 직접적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be said to adults too, but it is quite direct.

explain_en: It pairs with '쓰다' or '부리다' as '생떼를 쓰다/부리다', for insisting or begging stubbornly for something impossible. It feels more unreasonable than '떼를 쓰다' and can be used for adults as well as children.

examples.ko: 동료가 아무 이유 없이 제 보고서에 생트집을 잡아요.
examples.en: My coworker finds fault with my report for no reason at all.
It is hard to work with someone who only picks petty quarrels.

examples.ko: 이건 생트집 아니에요? 저는 잘못한 게 없어요.
examples.en: Isn't this just nitpicking? I did nothing wrong.
He tried to break the contract on a groundless pretext.
Don't respond to every one of those groundless complaints.

examples.ko: 그 말은 생트집이라서 신경 쓰지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: That comment was just nitpicking, so I decided to ignore it.

explain: '트집'에 비해 이유 없이 억지를 부리는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '생트집을 잡다'나 '생트집을 부리다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 상사가 이유 없이 제 일에 생트집을 잡아요.
phrases.en: My boss finds fault with my work for no reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 억지로 흠을 찾아 따질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for forcing a complaint out of nothing.

phrases.en: That customer kept making groundless complaints.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡다'보다 억지로 계속 우기는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like stubbornly keeping it up than '잡다'.

phrases.en: That's just unreasonable nitpicking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가의 불평이 억지라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone's complaint is unreasonable.

explain_en: Compared with '트집' (fault-finding), it has a stronger sense of making a groundless, forced complaint. It usually appears as '생트집을 잡다' or '생트집을 부리다'.

en: to pace around; to hang around

examples.ko: 약속 시간보다 일찍 와서 역 앞에서 서성댔어요.
examples.en: I arrived earlier than planned and hung around in front of the station.

examples.ko: 아이가 교문 앞에서 서성대는 걸 보고 말을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I saw a child lingering in front of the school gate and spoke to him.

examples.ko: 면접 전에 긴장돼서 복도를 서성대고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was nervous before the interview, so I was pacing the hallway.

examples.ko: 누가 집 앞에서 서성대서 좀 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Someone was loitering in front of my house, and it was a little scary.
Don't just hover there, come in and have a seat.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 병원 앞을 서성댄 사람은 그의 아버지였어요.
examples.en: The person who paced in front of the hospital all day was his father.

explain: '서성이다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 기다리거나 망설이며 한 곳 주변을 왔다 갔다 할 때 써요. 걷는 것이 목적인 '산책하다'와 달리 불안, 기다림, 망설임의 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: He lingered in front of the door for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서성대다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 서성대다, and used more often.

phrases.en: After hanging around for a while, I went inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-다가'로 서성이던 동작 다음에 다른 일이 이어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: -다가 connects the pacing to the action that follows.

phrases.en: Don't hang around outside, come in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 말고'로 그만하고 다른 행동을 하라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -지 말고 tells someone to stop and do something else.

explain_en: It is used with the same meaning as '서성이다'. It is for moving back and forth around one spot while waiting or hesitating. Unlike '산책하다', where walking is the point, it carries a feeling of anxiety, waiting or indecision.

t90.ax: Don't just hover there, come in and have a seat.

en: to settle or clean up (a situation); to recover (remains, belongings)

examples.ko: 사고가 나자 직원들이 서둘러 상황을 수습했어요.
examples.en: After the accident, the staff hurried to sort out the situation.
I made the mistake, so I'll clean it up myself.
The team leader stepped in to settle the fight.
I gathered up the scattered things and put them in my bag.

examples.ko: 문제가 커지기 전에 빨리 수습해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to handle the problem fast before it gets bigger.

examples.ko: 사장님이 사과문을 올리고 사태를 수습하고 있어요.
examples.en: The boss posted an apology and is dealing with the incident.

explain: 수습하다는 어지럽고 문제가 생긴 상황을 정리해서 바로잡는다는 느낌이에요. 사고, 실수, 싸움처럼 일이 꼬였을 때 자주 쓰고, 흩어진 물건을 모을 때도 써요. 일이 커지기 전에 마무리한다는 뜻이라 '사태를 수습하다'가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The team leader stepped up first and sorted out the situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 생긴 상황을 바로잡는다는 뜻의 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to set a troubled situation right.

phrases.example: 일이 너무 커져서 수습할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: Things have grown too big to be put right.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 수 없다'를 붙이면 이미 너무 꼬여서 바로잡기 어렵다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ㄹ 수 없다' it means things are already too tangled to fix.

phrases.en: I hurriedly gathered up the papers blown away by the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여기저기 흩어진 것을 모아 정리할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for collecting and tidying things scattered around.

explain_en: 수습하다 carries the feel of tidying up and fixing a messy or troubled situation. It is common after accidents, mistakes, or fights, and also for gathering scattered things. '사태를 수습하다' (bring a situation under control) appears often in the news.

t90.ax: I made the mistake, so I'll clean it up myself.

examples.en: A pickpocket suddenly snatched my bag.
When I jerked the fishing rod, a big fish came up.

examples.ko: 그는 내 손목을 잡아채서 밖으로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: He grabbed my wrist and pulled me outside.
A motorcycle came closer to snatch the bag.
Please don't take things as if you're snatching them.
The person who snatched the wallet ran away.

explain: 갑자기 힘을 주어 확 잡아당겨 가지는 동작이에요. 가방 날치기나 낚시에서 자주 나오고, '낚아채다'와 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: The child snatched the snack out of my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같은 말이고, 빠르게 가로채는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, with more of a quick-grab feeling.

phrases.en: I was startled when someone suddenly yanked my wrist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작을 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for describing the next action or result.

phrases.en: Please don't suddenly yank my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거친 행동을 하지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to grab roughly.

explain_en: To grab and pull sharply, like a bag or sleeve. It describes grabbing something and yanking it suddenly with force. It often appears in bag-snatching and fishing contexts, and is used much like '낚아채다'.

t90.ax: A pickpocket suddenly snatched my bag.

examples.en: Try wringing out the wet towel tightly.
I squeezed a lemon into the water.

examples.ko: 아무리 머리를 쥐어짜도 생각이 안 나요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I rack my brain, I can't remember.
If you wring out the laundry, a lot of water comes out.
The toothpaste was almost gone, so I squeezed out every last bit.
It hurt as if my heart were being wrung.

explain: '짜다'보다 손에 힘을 더 줘서 꽉 쥐고 누르는 느낌이에요. 수건이나 레몬 같은 물건에도 쓰고, '머리를 쥐어짜다'처럼 애써서 생각을 짜낼 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 머리를 쥐어짜서 겨우 아이디어를 하나 냈어요.
phrases.en: rack one's brain
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법이 안 떠오를 때 애써서 열심히 생각하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes thinking very hard when no idea comes easily.

explain_en: Grip and twist with the hand, strong force. Compared with 짜다, it feels like gripping and pressing harder with your hand. It is used for towels and lemons, and also for forcing out ideas, as in '머리를 쥐어짜다'.

t90.ax: I squeezed a lemon into the water.

examples.en: My friend gave me a telling-off for coming late.
How could you scold me first instead of helping?

examples.ko: 작은 실수에도 핀잔이 돌아와서 기분이 상했어요.
examples.en: Even a small mistake got me a rebuke, and it upset me.

examples.ko: 핀잔 섞인 말투 때문에 마음이 불편했어요.
examples.en: His scolding tone made me uncomfortable.
He answered with a smile even when he was rebuked.
I spoke up for no reason and just got told off.

explain: '핀잔을 주다'(하는 쪽)와 '핀잔을 듣다/먹다'(받는 쪽)를 짝으로 외워 두세요. '꾸중'이 윗사람이 크게 혼내는 느낌이라면, '핀잔'은 면박을 주듯 가볍게 말하는 느낌에 가까워요.

phrases.en: When his younger brother made a mistake, his older brother scolded him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 핀잔을 하는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person doing the telling-off.

phrases.en: I got told off for being late to the appointment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 핀잔을 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person receiving the rebuke.

phrases.example: 숙제를 안 해서 선생님께 핀잔을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I got scolded by my teacher for not doing my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '핀잔을 듣다'와 뜻은 같지만 더 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 핀잔을 듣다 but more colloquial.

explain_en: Learn '핀잔을 주다' (to give it) and '핀잔을 듣다/먹다' (to receive it) as a pair. While '꾸중' feels like an elder scolding someone seriously, '핀잔' is closer to a light putdown.

examples.ko: 어머니가 입원하셔서 제가 간병을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: My mother is in the hospital, so I am looking after her.
It is not easy to find a caregiver.

examples.ko: 간병 때문에 한 달 동안 휴가를 냈어요.
examples.en: I took a month off to take care of a patient.
I checked at the hospital how much caregiving costs.
I got really worn out taking care of my father.
The family decided to take turns caring for the patient.

explain: '간호'는 환자를 치료하며 돌보는 일까지 넓게 쓰고, '간병'은 환자 곁에서 먹고 씻는 것을 도우며 돌보는 일에 써요. '간병인', '간병비'처럼 함께 쓰는 말이 많아요.

phrases.example: 간병인이 하루 종일 할머니를 돌봐 드려요.
phrases.en: A caregiver looks after my grandmother all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자를 돌보는 일을 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person whose job is caring for a patient.

phrases.en: I'm worried because caregiving costs a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자를 돌보는 데 드는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the money spent on caring for a patient.

phrases.en: I've been caring for my father for several months now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 바꾸면 '간병을 하다'보다 짧고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it is shorter and more natural than 간병을 하다.
phrases.en_equiv: to nurse; to care for a patient

explain_en: Staying beside a sick person to care for them, often family or caregiver. '간호' (nursing) can include medical care, while '간병' means staying by a patient and helping with things like eating and washing. It appears in set words such as '간병인' (caregiver) and '간병비' (care costs).

t90.ax: It is not easy to find a caregiver.

examples.en: The mosquito bite keeps itching.
My throat tickled, so I drank some water.
My nose tickled, and then I sneezed.
My back is itchy. Can you scratch it for me?
My hair touched the back of my neck and it tickled.
As the wound healed, it began to itch.

explain: '간지럽다'가 일반적인 말이고, '간질거리다'는 간질간질한 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. 사람이 일부러 간지럽게 하는 건 '간질이다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My nose is tickling, so I'm sneezing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간지러운 느낌이 이어질 때 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for a continuing tickling feeling.

phrases.en: My back itched, so I scratched it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 말이고 어디서든 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic word, usable anywhere.

phrases.en: My eyes itch so much I can't stand it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형 '-아서'를 붙여 이유와 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아서 links a reason to a result.

explain_en: '간지럽다' is the general word, while '간질거리다' is used when the tickly feeling keeps going. When a person deliberately tickles someone, the word is '간질이다'.
